label: yes
controls_available: Pointer movement across the visible flight canvas sets a continuous normalized yaw/pitch steering vector in full mode.
The selected pointer vector persists until another pointer move; full mode renders no trim buttons.
The plane flies autonomously and seals are collected by world-space contact; the terminal result is submitted automatically.
autonomous_processes: Immediately after rendering, a requestAnimationFrame loop advances the flight in 40 ms physics ticks even without a new input; each tick turns the plane toward the persistent vector and advances its world-space x, y, and z position.

As the plane/camera advances, uncollected seals and scenery are reprojected into the visible camera frustum and seal apparent size changes with depth; world-space contact collects seals and leaving the corridor terminates the flight.
grouped_control_modes: D_full_pointer_steering: every full-mode pointer-vector correction across generated seeds, route approaches, and attempts, including corrections while an uncollected seal is visibly projected.
Persistent-vector hold/no-op: no new pointer move while the last steering vector continues to drive the flight; this is the no-op comparison for the full pointer mode.

clause_i.reason: At active seal approaches, the same prior action/timing history can occur for generated routes whose next seal is at different visible lateral or vertical positions. An observation-free q(I_t) must choose the same pointer vector for those histories, although their delayed-optimal vectors differ; the randomized route is not encoded in I_t.

clause_ii.reason: For the same full-pointer steering mode, the six chronological frames in the configured 600 ms window expose the visible seal projection, its drift relative to the fixed cockpit marker, and depth-dependent size change. A bounded visual policy can use that recent trajectory to predict the seal's position at t+600 ms and select the canvas yaw/pitch vector.

clause_iii.reason: For a visible off-axis seal in an active approach, a pointer vector aimed at that seal has higher value when delivered at t. With no new action, 40 ms ticks move and turn the plane; for some 0 < tau < 600 ms the seal's world-space crossing/alignment opportunity is already worse while later correction can still keep success possible. The same vector delivered at t+600 ms can arrive after the useful contact corridor or with a larger lateral/vertical error. This is non-clock flight-state evolution, not merely a deadline or later submission.

common_visible_process: The common process is forward 3D flight through static delivery seals: the persistent pointer vector changes the plane heading, each 40 ms tick advances the plane, and the camera reprojects the seals so their screen position and depth-dependent size visibly change across the recent frame window. That same visible trajectory determines the delayed pointer correction, while forward motion through a radius-10 world-space seal makes a presently useful correction degrade or expire during the delay.

pre_run.reason: There is no separate start gate: render resets the full-mode control to [0, 0] and immediately schedules the autonomous flight loop, while pointermove is the outcome-affecting control. With no outcome-affecting action during the autonomous phase, the plane remains on the zero-control trajectory. At difficulty 5 the first generated seal always has |x| at least 0.62*96 = 59.52 (and is forced to 0.86*96 when the random sample is nearer the center), whereas the world-space contact radius is 10; the straight initial flight therefore cannot contact the first seal in any generated instance. No percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 selects seven targets, spacing 80, lateral span 96, vertical span 72, flight speed 2.65, turn step 0.21, contact radius 10; full interaction is continuous pointer steering and the observation window is 600 ms with six frames.

The condition selects the requested difficulty profile; target depth progresses by spacing, lateral/vertical coordinates are randomized, successive waypoints change route heading, and the first target is forced away from the centerline.
Generated physics runs at tick_ms 40 with the difficulty-5 speed and contact radius, and the plane starts at x=y=z=yaw=pitch=0.
Full-mode pointer movement maps the canvas position to normalized yaw and pitch and persists the resulting control vector.
Each autonomous step turns toward the current control, advances the plane in 3D, checks world-space contact against the seal radius, and ends the flight on completion or corridor exit.
Seals are rendered as projected 3D spheres with screen position and depth-dependent size; only seals in the camera frustum are visible, while the plane remains a fixed cockpit marker.
The animation loop consumes elapsed time in 40 ms ticks, render resets control and state, full mode attaches pointermove to the canvas, and the loop starts immediately without a start gate.
The full canvas is the visible signed yaw/pitch pointer field and remains available as the flight interaction surface.
The grader binds the exact interaction mode to pointer_steer for full mode and independently replays the scheduled controls, plane motion, corridor, and world-space contacts with event ordering.

The implementation solver repeatedly re-observes the plane and next target and sends a new pointer move, which is evidence of closed-loop control rather than a pre-run action sequence; its private state is not treated as policy information.
The task verifier loads the exported result and the independent Cloudpost Circuit grader, so the authoritative outcome is the replayed world-space result.
